issues.description: noarch packages silently produce broken URLs
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url only matches x86_64/aarch64/ppc64le/s390x. The repoquery in generate_main uses '--arch noarch' to capture noarch packages, and these URLs will not match any pattern, causing the function to return None. The constructed URL becomes 'https://kojipkgs.fedoraproject.org/repos-dist/coreos-pool/latest/None/Packages/...' which is a broken URL silently inserted into the lockfile. Either 'noarch' must be added to the arches list, or None must raise an exception.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returns None with no error handling at call site
issues.detail: When the regex fails to match, the function returns None and use_koji_url_only happily formats it into the URL string via f-string interpolation. There is no validation, no log, no exception. Any URL that does not contain one of the four hard-coded arches will silently corrupt the lockfile. At minimum the caller should raise on None.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and koji tagging is unmitigated
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges that coreos-koji-tagger tags to coreos-pool only after the bump-lockfile commit merges, so URLs written by use_koji_url_only may 404 in the window before tagging completes. There is no retry, no verification, and no documentation in code about this. A comment in the source pointing to the operational assumption would help future maintainers, and ideally a verification step (HEAD request or post-merge gate) would close the gap.

issues.description: Local testability regression has no mitigation
issues.detail: The PR description acknowledges 'rpms.lock.yaml changes cannot be tested locally' because the koji tag operation is remote. This is a meaningful developer-experience regression. A --dry-run flag, a mock mode, or at least unit tests for use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url would partially compensate; none are added.

issues.description: No unit tests for new URL-construction logic
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url contain non-trivial string manipulation and regex logic that determines the contents of every lockfile entry. There are no tests covering coreos-pool passthrough, fedora-secondary substitution, noarch handling, package names starting with digits (e.g. 389-ds-base), or the None-return path. Given that local testing is now impossible, missing tests is a significant gap.

issues.description: Variable named 'nevra' actually holds the full RPM filename
issues.detail: url.split('/')[-1] yields something like 'kernel-6.5.0-1.fc39.x86_64.rpm', which is a filename, not a NEVRA. The code still works because the koji bucket directory is the first character of the filename (which equals the first character of the package name). Renaming to 'rpm_filename' would prevent confusion.

issues.description: koji_url_base membership check uses substring match
issues.detail: 'if koji_url_base in url' is a substring check. It works in practice because the base URL is distinctive, but a stricter url.startswith(koji_url_base) would be safer and clearer in intent.

issues.description: Arch list is hard-coded in two places conceptually
issues.detail: The arches ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] are hard-coded inside extract_arch_from_url. The set of supported arches is a project-wide concept; defining it as a module-level constant (and reusing the existing arch enumeration elsewhere in the file) would prevent drift if a new arch is added.
extract_arch_from_url compiles the same regex on every invocation. For a long lockfile this is wasteful. Hoist the compiled pattern to module scope.

The comment block about the dnf5 bug was removed but the prioritization logic ('if coreos-pool in url or not existing_url') remains. Now that use_koji_url_only rewrites every non-pool URL anyway, the upstream prioritization step is largely redundant. Consider whether it can be simplified or whether keeping it as a defense-in-depth measure should be documented with a fresh comment.

dissents.topic: How to handle a URL with no matching arch

positions.position: Returning None and letting the URL render as '.../None/...' is acceptable because in practice every fedora URL contains one of the four arches; failures will be loud at build time when the URL 404s.

Silent None-to-string interpolation is a correctness bug. The function should raise ValueError on no match (or the caller should), because a 404 at hermetic-build time is far more expensive to diagnose than an early exception with the offending URL.

dissents.topic: Whether to address the race condition in this PR

positions.position: The race is bounded (minutes), affects only Konflux, and the existing process tolerates it. Scope creep to add verification is unnecessary.

Crafting URLs that don't yet exist is a meaningful invariant change. At minimum a code comment documenting the assumption, and ideally a post-merge HEAD check, belongs in this PR so future contributors understand the contract.
Since rpms.lock.yaml is consumed only by Konflux, losing local reproducibility is acceptable; the PR description acknowledges this.
Even Konflux-only artifacts benefit from a --dry-run or offline mode. Loss of local testing materially slows future debugging and is worth a small mitigation in the same PR.

review.summary: The patch replaces a fragile dnf5-workaround with a deterministic URL-rewriter that points every package at coreos-pool. The approach is sound and the PR description honestly notes its two known downsides (race condition with koji tagging, loss of local testability). The most serious issue is that extract_arch_from_url returns None on no match and the caller interpolates that None directly into the URL — noarch packages (which the surrounding code explicitly requests via '--arch noarch') will silently produce broken '.../latest/None/Packages/...' URLs. Secondary concerns are the absence of any unit tests for new logic that now determines every lockfile entry, and minor cleanups (compiled regex hoisting, variable naming, redundant prioritization logic in query_packages_location). Recommend blocking on noarch handling and the None-return safety before merge.
